name: CA-47
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by 6 points on the PVI
Incumbent Dave Min holds a large financial advantage ($3.4M raised vs $0.4M)
Prediction markets price Min at 95-96% to win
model.rationale: The fundamentals point strongly to Min: a Democratic-leaning district, incumbency, and a roughly nine-to-one fundraising edge, while both Kalshi and Polymarket price him near 95% to win. With no contrary polling or ratings, the forecast stays close to the baseline margin of about 19 points.
model.watch: Any late polling showing Min underperforming the district's lean, or a surge of outside spending for Le Roux, would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Dave Min, the Democratic incumbent, is seeking a second term in a Southern California district that voted about six points more Democratic than the nation in recent cycles. He enters the general election with a commanding financial position, having raised roughly $3.4 million and holding $1.9 million on hand, while Republican Jenny Le Roux has raised under $400,000 and reports only $128,000 in cash. Outside spending in the race has been minimal so far.

No public general-election polls are available, and no expert raters have published ratings for the contest. Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price Min's chances at about 95 to 96 percent. With the fundamentals, money, and markets all aligned, the race is rated Safe Democratic, though the absence of polling leaves some room for uncertainty.
